entities.title: A name, not an email
entities.summary: The table asks for a name of up to 12 characters; no email or other personal data is collected.
entities.context: The table was first keyed by the player's email, stored privately, with the part before the @ shown.

options.title: Keep the email
options.consequences: Personal data stored for every reign.

options.title: Ask for a name
options.consequences: No personal data; the name is cleaned to what the game's font can draw.

entities.decision: A name, typed on an arcade-style entry screen and kept for the browser session; a signed-in player starts with the part of their email before the @, which is offered, not stored. The email column was dropped from the live database.

entities.title: Every screen waits for a key; timed screens move on after 7 s
entities.summary: The screens the original moved on by itself draw in full, hold for their old time, then wait for a key or 7 seconds.
entities.context: In playtesting a newsflash went by too fast to read. A later decision that day found that waiting indefinitely went too far the other way.

options.title: The original's timing
options.consequences: Some screens are gone before they can be read.

options.title: Every screen waits for a key
options.consequences: A reign stalls whenever the player looks away.

options.title: Hold, then wait for a key or 7 seconds
options.consequences: Readable, and the reign still moves.

entities.decision: A screen the original timed draws in full and plays its sound, ignoring keys, for at least its time in RULES §15.5, then shows the any-key footer; a key moves on at once, and with no key it moves on 7 seconds after it appeared (or when its own time ends, if later). Screens that ask something wait for their answer.
entities.rationale: The keys these screens read never change the game, so the change is invisible to the state and to parity.

entities.title: Every server call is best effort
entities.summary: The game plays without the server; only entering the table needs it.
entities.context: The game was first a static page with no server; the table added three calls.
entities.decision: startReign waits 3 s, submitReign 10 s, the table and /games/me 5 s and 3 s; any failure returns null. Without a seed the reign plays with a local one and is not offered to the table; without the table the screen says it can't be reached.
entities.rationale: A slow or absent server never stops a reign.
